# Brevi

> Brevi is a compiler built for AI coding agents: it turns ordinary Python into a fast, memory-safe native binary through Rust. Write plain Python (standard library or installed packages) and run it with `brevi run main.py`; there is no guide to read first. The program is compiled to native code, which runs plain loops over ints, lists and strings several times faster than CPython (1.7x to 39.5x, median 8.5x, on our 12 compute benchmarks), so write the plain, direct solution and do not hand-optimise it for speed. Brevi checks the whole program before it runs, reports sure mistakes (unknown names and methods, text plus a number) as one short JSON line with a suggested fix, and otherwise aims to print exactly what CPython prints. It is not there yet: on CPython 3.13's own tests 80% match, 12% are refused, and 3% still build and answer differently (on its tests of the most used standard-library modules, 45% match), so check programs that matter with `brevi verify x.py --input tests/`. When a Python file is off the typed fast path, one `{"path":...}` line on stderr says which path ran (dynamic, pybridge or CPython), and the line and function that caused it. From v0.27.0, `brevi run --verify main.py` checks the run against CPython and gives CPython's answer, with a `{"verify":"differs"}` line, whenever Brevi's differs; it is the recommended run for agents. `brevi check` gives its verdict in well under a second, and checking or running unchanged files again replays the cached result in about 10 ms (`--no-cache` builds from scratch).

## Docs

- [Agent skill](https://brevi-lang.org/skill.md): setup and the write, run, fix loop for coding agents. Start here.
- [For AI agents](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/agents.md): the MCP server's tools, the skill and plugin, and prompting advice.
- [Using Brevi](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/usage.md): commands, flags, error formats, which path ran (typed, dynamic, pybridge or CPython) and why, the CPython fallback, sandbox and GUI test mode.
- [Install](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/install.md): release binaries, the install script, Docker and building from source.
- [What works, and limits](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/compatibility.md): Python coverage, which standard-library functions run native on the typed or dynamic build, libraries and known gaps.
- [Architecture](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/architecture.md): how a source file becomes a native program.
- [Language guide](https://brevi-lang.org/guide.md): Brevi's own syntax, for .bv files only. Not needed to build Python.
- [Reference](https://brevi-lang.org/reference.md): details for string braces and format specs, list methods and Python spellings. Look up one name with `brevi guide WORD` instead of reading it all.
- [Libraries](https://brevi-lang.org/libraries.md): using other .bv files, Rust crates (`use sha2 "0.10"` plus `rust fn`) and Python (`py fn`) from Brevi.
- [Changelog](https://brevi-lang.org/docs/changelog.md): what changed in each release, and what is on main for the next.
- [Benchmarks](https://brevi-lang.org/bench.md): speed against CPython and cost per finished task, with method and raw logs.

## Tools

- [Compiler source](https://github.com/ets-public/brevi): Apache-2.0, written in Rust.
- [Agent platform templates](https://github.com/ets-public/brevi/tree/main/templates): run an agent's Python under Brevi's sandbox and limits on E2B, Daytona, Modal, Cloudflare Sandbox or Docker.
- Contact: support@brevi-lang.org (questions, licensing; bugs go to GitHub issues).

- [Full text](https://brevi-lang.org/llms-full.txt): the guide, reference, libraries and skill in one file.
